core_obligations: Show that X is locally Noetherian from local finite type over a locally Noetherian base (proof lines 5771-5774).
Show that X is quasi-compact using quasi-compactness of f and of Y (proof lines 5774-5775).
Show that X is quasi-separated using finite presentation and Noetherianness of Y (proof lines 5776-5782).
Conclude by the definition of a Noetherian algebraic space (proof lines 5783-5786).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: if f : X -> Y is of finite presentation over a scheme S and Y is Noetherian, then X is Noetherian (source lines 5762-5768). The proof checks the three conditions of the chapter's definition of a Noetherian algebraic space: local Noetherianness comes from local finite type over a locally Noetherian base, quasi-compactness from quasi-compactness of f over the quasi-compact Y, and quasi-separatedness from finite presentation plus quasi-separatedness of Y via the separated-over-separated statement.
